messages:
jess: heads-up — during the v2 rollout probe we saw a weird header-entropy pattern from a set of client SDKs. some requests flip between `X-Client-Version: 1.*` and `X-Client-Version: 2.*` over short bursts, which is causing sticky-route churn and quota double-counting.

alex: ugh. are those legit clients or test traffic?

jess: looks legit — mobile SDKs on flaky networks. they re-auth and sometimes fall back to old hostnames that send outdated headers. 3% of traffic but concentrated on a few tenants.

mike: quick thought: we should avoid immediate route switch on a single request. add a short affinity window (e.g., 30s) keyed by token+client-id, with a decay if we see consistent v2. keeps latency stable.

tara: agree, but watch quotas — if we lock affinity to v1, tenants who opt-in to v2 might get charged at old model rates. we need a console-visible mapping showing per-tenant active model version and effective per-token pricing.

jess: proposed policy: keep existing affinity for 20s after a header change, but still emit a telemetry event annotated with `header_entropy:true` and sample at 100% for 1 hour so we can validate. also create a per-tenant flag `compat.early_reroute` to allow manual override from console.

eva: +1 for telemetry. can we also tag the events with `fallback_reason=header_mismatch` and `previous_route=v1` so the optimizer folks can correlate quality regressions?

mike: yes. telemetry fields: `client_version`, `route_assigned`, `route_previous`, `affinity_window_s`, `sample_rate`. export to redwood-telemetry-prod/shipping.

alex: small UX ask — console should show a compact badge when a tenant has >1% entropy in last 24h with a link to the logs. we can reuse the rollout card UI but add an "escape hatch" control to force legacy routing.

tara: escape hatch should be time-limited and audited. add an expiry and reason field. also require 2FA for hitting that control in prod.

jess: agreed on audit & expiry. for canary we want auto-probe: 5% traffic gets v2 for new tenants, but only if `header_entropy < 0.5%` over 1h. if entropy high, halt canary and send an ops alert.

deploy-bot: deploy 4842.12 -> routing-service v2-canary started by jess at 4842123490

mike: one more thing — quota accounting. currently quota buckets are keyed by token+route. with sticky changes we risk double-debit window. solution: if route changes within 60s, credit back tokens charged on the previous route and reassign to the new route's billing plan. implement as a reconciliation job that runs every 10s for recent changes.

eva: reconcile job OK, but make it idempotent and rate-limited. we should also expose a per-request flag `billing_override=true` for internal retries to avoid loops.

alex: how about a CLI probe to reproduce? something like:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Client-Version: 2.0.0" \
  -H "X-Client-ID: mobile-42" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v2/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
then flip header and replay. can reproduce churn.

tara: can ops get an alert rule? idea: alert when `header_entropy > 1%` for any tenant with >100 reqs/min, and when reconcile backlog >1000 items.

jess: I'll draft the rollout PR with: affinity window default 20s (configurable), telemetry event schema, console badge + escape hatch spec, reconcile job sketch, and alert rules. will ping infra & billing for review.

mike: thanks — please include unit tests for billing reconciliation and a small load test for affinity window behavior.

eva: tagging for visibility: @infra @billing @devex.

alex: :thumbsup:

jess: PR linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/142 — comments welcome.

deploy-bot: PR 142 merged by jess at 4842123515

mike: merging this should buy us stability during the rollout. follow-up: 2-week telemetry review and decide on default affinity.

jess: yep — let's regroup after the 48h canary window.
